# The linear relation generated by both reciprocal branches has the entire odd sector as multivalued part

## Reciprocal relation

The most direct replacement for an impossible parity graph is the linear relation generated by

\[
\left(
\cosh(su),
-
\sinh(su)
\right)
\]

for all reciprocal parameters \(s\). Denote it by

\[
\mathcal R_{\rm rec}
\subset
\mathcal H_e
\oplus
\mathcal H_o.
\]

Unlike an operator graph, a linear relation may assign multiple odd outputs to the same even input.

## Multivalued part

The generators at \(s\) and \(-s\) are

\[
(
\cosh(su),-
\sinh(su)
),
\]

\[
(
\cosh(su),+
\sinh(su)
).
\]

Their difference is

\[
(
0,-2\sinh(su)
).
\]

Therefore

\[
\sinh(su)
\in
\operatorname{mul}
\mathcal R_{\rm rec}.
\]

for every \(s\), where

\[
\operatorname{mul}
\mathcal R
=
\{g:(0,g)\in\mathcal R\}.
\]

Expanding at the origin shows that the multivalued part contains every odd monomial:

\[
u,
u^3,
u^5,\ldots
\]

Hence, on the analytic core and after closure under the standard density hypotheses,

\[
\operatorname{mul}
\mathcal R_{\rm rec}
=
\mathcal H_o.
\]

## Consequence

Passing from the relation to a single-valued quotient requires dividing out its multivalued part. That quotient removes the whole odd sector.

But the odd sector carries the derivative channel

\[
X'(z)
\]

and therefore the oriented Clark current. Consequently, the unrestricted reciprocal relation is too large: its natural quotient destroys precisely the information needed for positivity.

## Required orientation

One must choose only one member of each reciprocal pair before taking a graph or quotient. Analytically, this is a Hardy orientation:

- one half-plane boundary value is primary;
- the reciprocal branch is recovered by adjoint reflection;
- the two branches are not admitted as independent graph generators.

Equivalently, branch orientation must be retained as input history rather than forgotten in the even projection.

## Control interpretation

Allowing both branches with identical even observation makes the controller maximally nondeterministic. Its unobservable input ambiguity spans the entire odd output channel.

A well-posed controller requires a causality choice. In this problem, causality is the Hardy half-plane orientation or stopped-history direction.

## Disposition

A multivalued reciprocal relation does not solve the admission problem. Without Hardy orientation, its multivalued part is the full odd sector and the Clark derivative channel is lost. The next constructor must therefore begin with an oriented Hardy branch, not with the symmetric reciprocal pair.
